gaps.sentence: ___ it rains all weekend, the ceremony will still be held outdoors.
gaps.explanation: 'Even if' concedes a possible (not yet real) condition.

gaps.sentence: She speaks fluent Mandarin; ___, she reads classical Chinese.
gaps.explanation: 'Moreover' adds a further, even more remarkable achievement.

gaps.sentence: You can borrow the car ___ you fill the tank afterwards.
gaps.explanation: 'As long as' = only if, setting a requirement for permission.

gaps.sentence: I'll take the job ___ they don't offer me any more money.
gaps.explanation: 'Even if' concedes a future possibility that will not change the decision.

gaps.sentence: ___ the theory is elegant, the data simply don't support it.
gaps.explanation: 'Even though' grants the fact (the theory is elegant) before contradicting it.

gaps.sentence: ___ you book soon, there won't be any seats left.
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if... not': if you don't book soon, no seats.

gaps.sentence: She looked ___ she hadn't slept for a week.
gaps.explanation: 'As though' = as if, describing how somebody appears.

gaps.sentence: We took the coast road ___ the motorway to enjoy the views.
gaps.explanation: 'Instead of + noun' marks the rejected alternative.
